newsitem.title: CHINA: China says child mortality down 27.5 percent.
newsitem.headline: China says child mortality down 27.5 percent.

text.p: China said on Friday it had cut its infant mortality rate by 27.5 percent in the past five years, but warned that a gap in development between urban and rural areas was the main problem facing child health care.

China's infant mortality rate was 36.4 per 1,000 in 1995, a drop of 27.5 percent compared with 1991's figure of 50.19 per 1,000, said a report by the National Working Committee for Women and Children.
"Indicators for the basic situation of children have shown positive results," committee vice-president Xu Zhijian told a news conference.
The death rate for children under age five had fallen to 44.5 per 1,000 from 61.03 per 1,000 during the five years, a drop of 27.1 percent, Xu said.
Child malnutrition had dropped by more than one-fifth to 15.8 percent in 1995 and vitamin A deficiency had been nearly wiped out, he said.
China had made progress in immunising children and reducing incidence of often deadly child diseases such as measles and polio, he said.
By the end of 1995, China had immunised 85 percent of children down to the township level, he said.
"With necessary funding being provided, the work for children's well-being has gained an all-round development," he said.
But Xu warned that more work was needed in China's rural and western frontier regions, where economic growth has lagged far behind thriving eastern coastal areas.
"A great disparity of economic and social development exists in different regions and the well-being of children is not even as well," he said.
China was a developing country with a relatively low average annual per-capita income, he said, adding that this posed pressing problems to the well-being of children, he said.
"In the western poor regions of China, the infant and under-five mortality rate and the maternal mortality rate are greater than the national average," he said.
The committee's report said that while the infant mortality rate in urban areas was 14.2 per 1,000, in the countryside it was 41.6 per 1,000.
The urban under-five mortality rate was 16.4 per 1,000 compared to 51.1 per 1,000 in cities, the report said.

In developed coastal areas, the infant mortality rate was 25.6 per 1,000, while in central China the figure rose to 49.6 per 1,000. It shot to 85.4 per 1,000 in the remote, backward and sparsely populated west, the report showed.
Chinese President Jiang Zemin this week launched a high-profile campaign to lift out of destitution the 65 million people Beijing says fall below its official poverty line.
